Synagogenplatz Memorial in Wittmund

Memorial · Wittmund, Germany

Wittmund's Jewish congregation inaugurated a simple brick synagogue on 9 February 1816. It remained in use into the National Socialist period, but the shrinking community sold it in June 1938. The purchaser then demolished the building before the November pogrom. A memorial plaque now identifies the former synagogue property, and black basalt stones mark the building's outline between Kirchstraße 10 and 12. Because the synagogue no longer survives and the mapped feature is the commemorative Synagogenplatz, this record is classified as a memorial at a destroyed synagogue site.
